description: Single-user, single-routine-DSH-Agent, natural-language-first ChatGPT Web Planner -> explicit approval -> DSH Agent -> independent ChatGPT Web Reviewer loop. Internal structured validation and evidence are retained; manual JSON commands and project ZIP/Bridge attachments are not default user interaction. The actual cross-system handoff remains subject to live verification.

userStories.title: Initiate and authorize development using natural language
userStories.description: One user describes a task and receives a scoped ChatGPT Web plan in ordinary language. The Controller validates a machine-readable representation internally; the user need not construct JSON, IDs, or hashes.
acceptanceCriteria: A normal task and workflow approval can be completed without the user manually composing protocol JSON, run IDs, or SHA-256 fields.
A proposed plan identifies scope, checks, and stop conditions before the user authorizes execution.
Missing or mismatched authorization cannot trigger DSH execution.

userStories.title: Read relevant context without ZIPs or routine extra worktrees
userStories.description: ChatGPT Web inspects pushed code by the designated GitHub dev ref and relevant unpushed state through an authorized local connection. The normal workflow uses one configured local workspace and one active branch rather than automatically creating per-task environments.
acceptanceCriteria: The Planner and Reviewer record actual repository, branch/commit, and relevant local context source or an explicit visibility limitation.
Normal task context transfer does not require generation, upload, or return of project ZIPs or Bridge attachment descriptors.
Routine tasks do not create another worktree, branch, or dependency installation unless isolation is justified and separately authorized.

userStories.title: Execute only through the configured DSH Agent and approvals
userStories.description: DSH Agent is the sole routine development and test executor. Trusted Host configuration selects the project root, provider/model and native tool permissions. Model names describe current implementation, not permanent product obligations.
acceptanceCriteria: An approved task executes only via the DSH Agent and its configured tools in the trusted workspace.
DSH native workspace permissions and approval policy are independent of workflow plan approval; rejected or missing approval fails closed without shell or connector fallback.
No automatic commit, push, merge, reset, or clean occurs without separate express authorization.

userStories.title: Return auditable evidence and independent review without user-written JSON
userStories.description: Controller keeps run/approval/evidence linkage in internal structured records while ChatGPT Web independently checks actual Git delta, DSH tool/test results and project state. Non-accepted conclusions do not automatically rerun.
acceptanceCriteria: Relevant actual files, diff, DSH tool approval outcomes, test command/results, and execution finalization are bound to the run and available for independent review.
Tampered, mismatched, stale or incomplete evidence is rejected; the Reviewer cannot claim completion from model report alone.
User-facing review and follow-up are ordinary-language summaries; any internal JSON contract is generated or consumed by tooling rather than typed by the user.

userStories.title: Verify a real small end-to-end natural-language development loop
userStories.description: With separate explicit authorization, run one real bounded ChatGPT Web planning, approval, DSH Agent development and testing, and ChatGPT Web independent review on a controlled project. Do not infer automatic app handoff capability from connector availability.
acceptanceCriteria: One separately authorized real run records plan approval, actual DSH Agent tool and test evidence, Git changes, Reviewer verification and a correlated terminal outcome.
The user completes the normal interaction without constructing JSON or ZIPs; any still-human-mediated cross-system handoff is clearly identified and evaluated rather than silently called automated.
Deterministic offline tests or unverified model reports alone do not count as completion of real M2 acceptance.
